subject: Energy
title: The Third Law of Thermodynamics
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Third Law of Thermodynamics usable.

hook.text: Absolute zero (−273.15°C) is the coldest possible temperature—where atomic motion nearly stops.

buildup.text: The third law says you can never actually reach absolute zero—you can only approach it asymptotically.

discovery.text: At absolute zero, a perfect crystal would have zero entropy—perfect order with no randomness at all.

twist.text: Scientists have cooled atoms to billionths of a degree above zero—but true zero remains forever unreachable.

climax.text: Near absolute zero, bizarre quantum effects emerge—superfluids flow without friction and metals become superconductors.

punchline.text: You can chase absolute zero forever—but never arrive.

quiz.question: What happens at absolute zero according to the third law?
options: A perfect crystal has zero entropy
